title: kv-cache: adaptive-defrag + spillover eviction heuristics v23 (reduce fragmentation & paging)
author: Priya Patel
release_notes: Improves KV cache memory management: adaptive defragmentation, spillover-aware eviction priority, paging threshold tuning. Reduces memory churn and tail latency under mixed-length workloads. No API changes.
description: Motivation: we continue to see KV cache fragmentation and excessive paging under mixed long/short sequence workloads which increases GPU memory churn and tail latency during spillover. This change implements an adaptive defragmentation pass combined with spillover-aware eviction heuristics to reduce page churn, prioritize eviction candidates that minimize compaction cost, and adjust paging thresholds dynamically by observed access patterns. Key changes: 1) new DefragWorker that runs opportunistic compaction when fragmentation ratio crosses a tunable threshold; 2) adaptive eviction priority that scores entries by last-access, size, and defrag-cost-estimate rather than simple LRU; 3) spillover scheduler that groups low-benefit entries for paged-out storage and batches page-ins to reduce IO spikes; 4) runtime knobs and feature flags (kv.defrag.enabled, kv.defrag.threshold, kv.spillover.batch_ms) to allow gradual rollout and safe rollback; 5) microbenchmarks and integration tests that simulate mixed-length chat+completion workloads and long-context LVKV stress tests. Backwards compatibility: internal API unchanged; default behavior rolled out behind feature flag and config defaults tuned to current production values. Observed results in our benchmark lab: median token throughput unchanged, 95th-percentile memory churn reduced by ~28%, tail latency (p99 token generation) reduced by ~12% under mixed workloads, and peak paging IO reduced by ~35% in synthetic traces. This PR includes unit tests for scoring logic, e2e integration tests across small/medium/large model weights, and updated runtime metrics (kv.fragmentation_ratio, kv.defrag_runs, kv.spill_pages, kv.eviction_score_distribution). Linear references: ENG-2345 (kv-cache memory improvements), ENG-2399 (runtime perf validation).

review_comments: Ethan Kim: Can you clarify how defrag cost is estimated at runtime? Concerned about CPU overhead when scanning metadata.

Priya Patel: We estimate cost using a lightweight summary collected at allocation/free time (fragment size histogram + stale-run counters) and limit scans to hot shards; added microbenchmarks showing <1% CPU at 99th percentile.
Lena Ortiz: Please make sure spillover batching doesn't increase latency for interactive traffic; suggest a safeguard to prioritize low-latency routes.
Priya Patel: Added route-aware spillover prioritization and a fast-path that bypasses batching for latency-sensitive routes; tests added to validate.
Marco Ruiz: Left a nit on config naming and asked for a short rationale in docs for choosing defaults.
Priya Patel: Renamed kv.defrag.threshold -> kv.defrag.fragmentation_threshold and updated docs with rationale and benchmark numbers.
Ethan Kim: Approving after CI green and bench numbers included in the PR description.
Lena Ortiz: Approved and requested backport candidate label for stable release.
notes: Feature rolled out behind kv.defrag.enabled feature flag; operations scheduled a canary rollout to Dedicated clusters over 2 weeks.
benchmarks_summary: Mixed-length synthetic lab: 95p memory churn -28%, p99 token latency -12%, peak paging IO -35% compared to baseline; throughput steady across model sizes.
